No session yet. Aim the camera, check the schedule, then tap Start.
Phone time: %1$s. Check it before a field session: the session record uses it.
The camera closes; the photos and videos so far are kept.
Square: %1$d %% of the short side of the photo, %2$s. Only the square is saved; focus and exposure follow it. %3$s
Shows the camera view, to point the phone at the flower. Video saves the whole view. %1$s
Photos: one every %1$s s for %2$s s, then %3$s min off.
Photos: one every %1$s s, without breaks.
Video %1$s, %2$d frames per s: clips of %3$s min, then %4$s min off.
Video %1$s, %2$d frames per s: clips of %3$s min, one after the other.
Time between photos in a burst. Default 2 s: a 3 s step caught about 90 % of insect visits (Edwards et al. 2015).
Default 60 s: longer than a typical visit (about 11 s).

The square is shrunk to this size when saved. Default 1280 px: the input size of many insect detectors, so they need no resizing (all three are multiples of 32). A square with fewer real pixels is never enlarged: it is saved at its own size, rounded down to a multiple of 32.
One video file per clip. Default 5 min.
On the Samsung M12, one hour of video at 5 frames per s took about 2.2 GB at 1080p, 1.2 GB at 720p and 0.6 GB at 480p.

Default 5: enough to follow insects from frame to frame on a computer. Use 10 or 15 for fast flying insects. Fewer frames give smaller files, but not in proportion: on the Samsung M12, 5 frames per s took about 55 % of the storage of 15, and 10 about 80 %.
Default 4 min: the camera rests about 80 % of the time. It is switched off when the break is longer than 30 s. 0 = no break.
Default 2 h. Up to 720 h (30 days) without a break at night, for example under the midnight sun.

Clock times, for example 06:00-08:00, 17:00-20:00. A window may cross midnight (22:00-04:00), and 00:00-24:00 records all day (for example under the midnight sun). Default 05:00-21:00: early morning and evening visits count (Toivonen and Humberg 2026).
Default 1. Counted from the first window that is not over yet: a phone started in the evening records from the next morning. For more days, keep the phone on a power supply.

The camera stays off until the battery is 3 °C cooler. Default 45 °C: phones still work, but most stop charging near 45 °C and the battery wears fast above it. At most 50 °C. The session also stops cleanly when the battery falls to 15 % without charging, or when the storage is nearly full.
A short name such as P1 or Meadow-3 (letters a to z, digits, - or _). It is added to the session folder name and the record, so files from several phones do not mix. Default values keep it.
After Start, switch the screen off with the power button: the session goes on. Files are saved in %1$s.
This is the app\'s own folder: Android deletes it when the app is uninstalled. Allow the storage permission to save in Documents/FaunaLapse instead.
Square side (% of the short side of the photo)
Square: %1$d %% of the short side, %2$d px across in the full photo, saved at %3$d px. %4$s, photo %5$s.
This is fewer than the saved side of %1$d px: the square is saved smaller, never enlarged. Make the square larger for more pixels on the insect.
Video %1$s (frames per s: %2$d); the whole view is saved. %3$s.
Lens position: %1$d of 100, from near to far (this phone does not tell the distance).
Auto: the camera focuses on the square at the start of each burst, then the lens stays. In a dense flower patch it may focus on another flower; Fixed avoids this.
Auto: the camera focuses on the middle of the view at the start of each clip, then the lens stays. In a dense flower patch it may focus on another flower; Fixed avoids this.

Fixed (default, starts at about 20 cm, a usual distance from phone to flower): the lens stays at this distance for the whole session and never focuses by itself, so bursts start faster, and wind, a passing insect or another flower cannot pull the focus away. Tap Focus again to focus once and fix the focus there, then adjust with the slider while you watch the view. Keep the phone where it is.

This phone cannot fix the focus: it focuses automatically on the square at the start of each burst or clip. In a dense flower patch, make the square cover mostly the target flower, so the camera focuses on it.
Focus: automatic at the start of each burst or clip.
Focus: fixed at %1$s; check it on the aim screen.
Focus: fixed at one lens position, set on the aim screen.
Focus: automatic at the start of each burst or clip, because this phone cannot fix the focus.

Drag the square onto the flower with a finger; pinch it with two fingers (or use the slider) to make it larger or smaller. The small triangle marks the top of the saved photos: it moves to the side when you hold the phone sideways, and stays at the top while the phone is upright or lies flat. Fix the phone in its place, then tap Start session here: the session uses this position.
Fix the phone in its place, then tap Start session here.

Tests with the back camera, without a preview.

One test photo: the camera opens, waits 5 s for the exposure, focuses once, takes one photo and closes.

Speed test (about 3 minutes): photos one after the other, photos from preview frames, short videos, and Camera2 photos.

The camera starts %1$d s after the tap, so you can switch the screen off first. Results are saved in:
%2$s
Working: the camera starts %1$d s after the tap and closes again when the test ends.
FaunaLapse needs the camera permission to take photos. Tap the button again to allow it.
